E047-01.notes: Colon after the independent clause correctly introduces the appositive explanation 'a lens that would bend...'. B: semicolon followed by a noun phrase fragment. C: 'A lens that would bend the light rather than reflect it.' is a fragment. D: comma splice ('approach, it was a lens').

E047-02.notes: 'Heavy' already means heavy in weight. A: redundant 'in weight'. B: redundant 'heavy and weighty'. D: wordy and redundant, plus an awkward stray comma before 'and difficult to cast'. C reads cleanly: 'would have been extremely heavy and difficult to cast.'

E047-03.notes: A comparison needs 'than'. A: 'then' is the time word. B: still uses 'then', and 'that of' adds a faulty comparison (lens vs. 'that of a solid lens'). C: 'far lighter as a solid lens' is not idiomatic; the comparative needs 'than'.

E047-04.notes: The opening modifier 'Arranged in rings around a central lens' must describe the prisms, so 'each prism' has to be the subject right after it. B: says Fresnel was arranged in rings (dangling modifier). C: dangling after 'there was'. It also changes the meaning to a single prism. D: the modifier attaches to 'the job', and the wording is wordy.

E047-05.notes: The sentence is a geographic aside that interrupts the move from the installation (8) to its dramatic effect (9-10). A: the sentence does not say why Cordouan was chosen. C: it says nothing about how far the light could be seen. D: it does not contradict anything, since the island is in France. Facts check out: Cordouan stands on a rocky islet or plateau at the mouth of the Gironde estuary, in southwestern France.

E047-06.notes: Sentence 10 gives a concrete example of the 'dramatic' improvement, so 'For instance' fits. A and B: they signal contrast or concession, but nothing in 10 opposes 9. D: 'Instead' signals a replacement that does not exist.

flags.note: B is the only option that agrees with the plural subject 'lenses', so agreement alone settles the item and tense never comes into play. The more natural 'were installed' is not offered. This is acceptable but makes the item a little easier than it looks.

E047-07.notes: The subject is the plural 'Fresnel lenses'. A ('has been'), C ('was') and D ('is') are all singular, and D is also the wrong tense for a past narrative. 'Had been installed' agrees with the subject, and the past perfect fits 'within a few decades' of 1823.

E047-08.notes: Possessive of the singular 'each lighthouse' = 'its'. A: 'it's' means 'it is'. B: 'its'' is not a word. C: 'their' does not agree with the singular antecedent 'each lighthouse'.

E047-09.notes: The clause shows that Fresnel was an expert in how light bends, which explains why he could propose a lens that bends light. A: the clause says nothing about manufacturing. B: soot is mentioned in sentence 2, not in this clause. D: no other physicists are mentioned.

E047-10.notes: The essay sets up a problem (wasteful, heavy mirrors and lenses), presents Fresnel's prism lens, and shows the result. A: the essay does not list lighthouses. C: the keepers are mentioned only once. D: false, because sentence 6 explains how the prisms bend light into a beam.

flags.note: The answer choices have no terminal periods, while the other keep/delete items in this batch (E047-05) end theirs with periods. This is a formatting inconsistency only.

E047-11.notes: The phrase gives the brand name, 'Craft Master'. A: it explains nothing about why sales improved. C: the name does not appear earlier in the essay. D: no contradiction, since sales improved later.

E047-12.notes: The order 4 (Klein doubtful at first), 5 (early kits sold poorly), 6 (sales improved after a demonstration) is logical. B: poor early sales would come after the improvement. C: 'early kits sold poorly' would come after 'millions of kits a year'. D: 'Early kits sold poorly' would follow sentence 3's description of the kit, and the 'at first' doubt would come after the sales results. This breaks the order of the narrative and is weaker than A.
